Getting started with gristmillr

Source: vignettes/gristmillr.Rmd
gristmillr.Rmd

gristmillr reads and writes Grist documents through the REST API. Functions take a document handle first, take and return data frames, and work in pipelines. The examples need a Grist account, so they are not run here.

Authenticate

gristmillr needs an API key, which you can create in Grist under Profile settings. The simplest setup is two environment variables in your .Renviron (see usethis::edit_r_environ()):

GRIST_API_KEY=<your key>
GRIST_SERVER=https://myteam.getgrist.com

GRIST_SERVER defaults to https://docs.getgrist.com. For a self-hosted site, include the team path if needed, e.g. http://localhost:8484/o/docs.

You can also pass the key directly, as a string or as a function that looks it up each time (handy with a keyring):

library(gristmillr)

doc <- grist_doc("<doc id>", api_key = \() keyring::key_get("grist"))

A key given as a string is held in memory for the session and is never saved with the object, so saving a handle with saveRDS() or in a targets pipeline doesn’t write your key to disk. Use the function form for handles you persist.

Find a document

grist_doc() accepts a document ID or the URL of a document, and the handle remembers the server:

doc <- grist_doc("https://myteam.getgrist.com/doc/<doc id>")
doc

If you don’t know the ID, list what you can see:

grist_orgs()
grist_workspaces("current")
grist_docs("current")

grist_doc_info(doc)

You can also create documents with grist_doc_create(), which returns a handle, or from a file with grist_doc_import(). It reads .grist, .csv, .xlsx and .json files and guesses column types from the values:

doc <- grist_doc_import("pets.csv", workspace = 1234, name = "Pets")

For several related tables, see vignette("migrating-data").

Read data 

grist_tables(doc)
grist_columns(doc, "People")

grist_records(doc, "People")

Filter and sort on the server, and limit the number of rows:

doc |>
  grist_records(
    "People",
    filter = list(status = c("active", "pending")),
    sort = "-age",
    limit = 100
  )

For anything more involved, run SQL (SELECT only):

grist_sql(doc, "SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM People GROUP BY status")
grist_count(doc, "People")

Column types

The convert argument controls how Grist cell values become R vectors:

  • "auto" (the default) reads the table’s column types, so Int becomes integer, Date becomes Date, DateTime becomes POSIXct, and ChoiceList and RefList become list-columns. It costs one extra request per call.
  • "basic" simplifies the JSON without looking up column types. Dates stay as numbers (seconds since 1970).
  • "raw" returns the API’s values unchanged.

Ref columns hold the row id of a record in another table. See vignette("joining-tables") for resolving and joining them.

Write data

Writes take a data frame and are converted the same way:

new <- data.frame(name = c("Ann", "Bob"), age = c(31L, 45L))
ids <- grist_records_add(doc, "People", new)

# Returns the new row IDs. Updates need an `id` column
grist_records_update(doc, "People", data.frame(id = ids[[1]], age = 32L))

grist_records_delete(doc, "People", ids)

To match on a column rather than the row id, use grist_records_upsert(). It updates records whose by values match and adds the rest, and never deletes anything. mode = "update" or "insert" limits it to one of the two, and onmany says what to do if several records match one row.

latest <- data.frame(name = c("Ann", "Cy"), age = c(32L, 28L))
grist_records_upsert(doc, "People", latest, by = "name")

Large writes are sent in chunks. With convert = "auto", a column that doesn’t exist in the table is an error, so typos surface before anything is sent.

Change the schema 

grist_table_create(doc, "Pets", c(name = "Text", age = "Int"))

grist_columns_add(doc, "Pets", c(owner = "Ref:People", adopted = "Date"))
grist_columns_modify(doc, "Pets", data.frame(id = "age", description = "In years"))

Settings

Rarely changed settings live in small option objects, so function signatures stay short:

doc <- grist_doc("<doc id>", options = grist_request_options(timeout = 60))

grist_records(doc, "People", options = grist_read_options(col_names = "label"))
grist_records_add(doc, "People", new, options = grist_write_options(chunk_size = 100))

Set defaults for a whole session with options(gristmillr.request_options = ..., gristmillr.read_options = ..., gristmillr.write_options = ...).

Deleting safely

Functions that delete things, such as grist_doc_delete() and grist_workspace_delete(), take mode = "trash" (the default, recoverable) or "permanent". In an interactive session they ask for confirmation. In a script they refuse to run unless you pass ask = FALSE.

doc |> grist_doc_delete()
doc |> grist_doc_restore()

Other features

  • Download documents or tables with grist_doc_download().
  • Manage attachments with grist_attachments*() and webhooks with grist_webhook*().
  • Review changes with grist_doc_history(), grist_snapshots() and grist_doc_compare().

For an endpoint gristmillr doesn’t wrap, grist_request() returns an authenticated httr2 request:

grist_request(doc, "tables") |>
  httr2::req_perform() |>
  httr2::resp_body_json()
